newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds open flat, traders focus on currency.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds open flat, traders focus on currency.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened little changed on Friday, with trading volumes light and an early close planned for the market ahead of the Victoria Day holiday weekend, analysts said.

"The market is focusing on the dollar, how much more it's going to run up. I don't think people are really sure how much more upside it has," said Sheldon Dong, manager of fixed-income research with Midland Walwyn Capital Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.05 to C$111.45 to yield 7.035 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 5/32 to yield 6.90 percent. The spread between the bonds was 14 basis points, unchanged from the close of trading on Thursday.

Canadian bonds rallied sharply yesterday and outperformed their U.S. counterparts as the Canadian dollar made its biggest one-day gains since 1994. Canadian bonds have managed to maintain those gains as the Canadian dollar firmed further overnight.
The dollar opened stronger at C$1.3660 (US$0.7320) this morning. The unit continues to benefit from signs that the Bank of Canada is preparing to tighten monetary policy.
Canadian bonds are expected to trade in a sideways fashion for the remainder of the session.

The Toronto Bond Traders' Association on Friday said it was recommending an early close for the market ahead of the Victoria Day long weekend. The association is recommending that the market cease trading at 1200 EDT/1600 GMT. The move effectively means an early close to bond market across Canada, as most bond traders are located in Toronto.
"This market will just be dead by the afternoon," said Dong.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.05 to C$103.45 to yield 6.508 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 5/32 to yield 6.69 percent.
The negative spread between the two bonds narrowed to 18 basis points from 19 basis points at the close of trading on Thursday.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 3.01 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.18 percent.
